summary: PARTIAL is right: #710 (60633eff3) added per-phase startup deadlines with actionable messages for ACP (Cursor, Grok, registry), Codex and Claude, plus a PATH-based cursor-agent preference. The auditor got the Cursor part wrong in two ways. First, #710 already verifies the binary's identity at probe time (isCursorAgentAboutOutput on `about` output), and model pickers only offer 'ready' instances, so a foreign `agent` is kept out of new sessions. Second, the auditor missed callers the fix does not cover: the Cursor maintenance update still runs a bare `agent update`, which on this machine resolves to ~/.grok/bin/agent first. Also missed: the registry ACP runtime's older 30 s whole-start cap hides the new phase budgets and messages. Still open: no client-visible phase reporting, 180 s text generation on commit/PR paths (tracked by the textgen finding), and Copilot start has no phase deadline.

evidence.note: DEFAULT_ACP_STARTUP_PHASE_TIMEOUTS: initialize 20 s, authenticate 20 s, session/new 30 s, session/load 60 s. withStartupPhaseDeadline (:485) wraps initialize (:520), authenticate (:560), session/new (:588) and session/load|resume (:621). Timed-out phases are not retried (:597, :633).

Codex phases: initialize 15 s, thread/start 30 s, thread/resume 60 s, applied at :2224/:2233. CodexAdapter.ts:2157 maps them to ProviderAdapterRequestError with the actionable detail. Covered by CodexStartupDeadline.integration.test.ts.

awaitCliInitialized applies a 30 s CLAUDE_STARTUP_INITIALIZE_TIMEOUT_MS (:232) at the top of sendTurnOnContext (:5956), stops the hung CLI and returns an actionable message (tested at ClaudeAdapter.test.ts:4937).
mapAcpToAdapterError passes AcpTransportError.detail through, so the phase message reaches the user for Cursor/ACP/Grok session starts.

MISSED BY AUDITOR: isCursorAgentAboutOutput, added in #710, checks who answered `about` and is used at :1055 to mark a foreign `agent` as not installed/error ('did not identify as the Cursor Agent CLI'). Tested at CursorProvider.test.ts:441. packages/client-runtime/src/state/composer/providerInstances.ts:161 offers only status==='ready' instances in pickers.
resolveCursorAgentCommand prefers cursor-agent when binaryPath is the default 'agent'. Used for sessions/textgen (CursorAcpSupport.ts:56) and probes (CursorProvider.ts:1001).

UNCOVERED CALLER: the maintenance update is hardcoded as `agent update` and run as a bare command by providerMaintenanceRunner.ts:354. Locally `which -a agent` gives ~/.grok/bin/agent (-> grok-1.0.44 binary) before ~/.local/bin/agent, so 'Update Cursor' runs the Grok binary.
The lab-channel hint hardcodes `agent set-channel lab && agent update`. The :1033 not-installed message and cliSetup/machine.ts:23 (labels any `agent` on PATH as Cursor) also ignore the resolver.
isCursorAgentAboutOutput accepts 'unknown command'/'unexpected argument' output as an old Cursor build, so a foreign CLI that rejects `about` that way passes as Cursor (with only a warning status).

Older code (17bcd353b): registry runtime.start() is capped at 30 s overall with the generic 'ACP agent startup timed out after 30 seconds.'. The new 60 s session/load budget can never apply to registry agents (strictResume). A session/new hang (30 s phase deadline, starting after initialize+auth) always surfaces with the generic text.

DEFAULT_REGISTRY_SESSION_START_TIMEOUT_MS = 300 s with 'may download its agent on first run', but resolveAcpRegistryInstallation (AcpRegistrySupport.ts:9-23) only resolves an explicitly installed agent, so both the value and the comment are stale.
progress.phase (lock/admission/adapter) is still used only for the timeout text (:1598). Admission stays at 4 concurrent starts per instance (:135).

session.state.changed with state 'starting' produces no activity, and its reason is never projected. Contracts have no session status-detail field, so even Codex's static 'session/connecting' reason (CodexSessionRuntime.ts:2223 -> CodexAdapter.ts:1132) never reaches the UI. Cursor/ACP adapters emit only 'ready' (CursorAdapter.ts:1005, AcpAdapter.ts:778).
Copilot createSession/resumeSession (retried once at :302) has no phase deadline. A hung Copilot CLI is bounded only by the 120 s session-start deadline with generic text.

Full-length text generation timeout is still 180 s (also ClaudeTextGeneration.ts:58, CursorTextGeneration.ts:35, GrokTextGeneration.ts:41). The naming/summary paths are 30 s (CodexTextGeneration.ts:52, ClaudeTextGeneration.ts:63, CursorTextGeneration.ts:37, GrokTextGeneration.ts:43). The finding defers this to the textgen finding.

remaining: 1) Client-visible startup phase reporting is absent. Phase deadlines (AcpSessionRuntime.ts:485, CodexSessionRuntime.ts:205, ClaudeAdapter.ts:5925) emit nothing. ProviderRuntimeIngestion.ts:556 drops 'starting' reasons, and there is no contracts field to carry one. The user sees a plain working state for up to 15-30 s before the actionable error. 2) Cursor wrong-binary is fixed for session, probe and textgen spawns, and the probe already does an identity check, which the auditor said was missing. Still uncovered: the maintenance update `agent update` (CursorDriver.ts:48 -> providerMaintenanceRunner.ts:354), which runs ~/.grok/bin/agent on this machine; the hardcoded `agent` in user-facing hints (CursorProvider.ts:790, :1033); setup detection (cliSetup/machine.ts:23); and the permissive 'unknown command' identity heuristic (CursorProvider.ts:745). The schema default stays 'agent' (packages/contracts/src/settings.ts:323). With the resolver that is acceptable, so do not change it. 3) Text generation keeps 180 s full-length timeouts (CodexTextGeneration.ts:47, ClaudeTextGeneration.ts:58, CursorTextGeneration.ts:35, GrokTextGeneration.ts:41). This is deferred to the textgen finding, and lowering them needs a slow-model decision there. 4) Copilot start (CopilotAdapter.session.ts:272-302) has no phase deadline. That provider is outside the proposal's list but has the same failure mode. 5) Admission of 4 starts per instance (ProviderService.ts:135) is unchanged. It is now bounded by the phase deadlines, so this is low priority.
fixDefects: (a) Uncovered caller of the Cursor collision fix: CursorDriver.ts:45-51 builds static maintenance capabilities with updateExecutable 'agent'. Update runs a bare `agent update` (providerMaintenanceRunner.ts:354) and bypasses resolveCursorAgentCommand. On this machine `which -a agent` resolves ~/.grok/bin/agent first, so Update Cursor executes the Grok binary. The hint at CursorProvider.ts:790 tells users to run `agent set-channel lab && agent update`, with the same problem. (b) Registry ACP: the older 30 s whole-start cap (AcpRegistrySupport.ts:66-78) masks the new phase deadlines. session/load|resume can never get its intended 60 s, and session/new or late authenticate hangs surface with the generic 'ACP agent startup timed out after 30 seconds.' instead of the actionable phase message. DEFAULT_REGISTRY_SESSION_START_TIMEOUT_MS = 300 s (providerOperationPolicy.ts:26) and its 'may download on first run' comment are stale. (c) Phase deadlines are fixed constants with no env knob, unlike RYCO_PROVIDER_*_TIMEOUT_MS, so very slow machines cannot raise them.
implementationSketch: A) Cursor update/hints (S, do first). In CursorDriver.ts, replace the static MAINTENANCE_CAPABILITIES (:45) with an Effect that runs resolveCursorAgentCommand(effectiveConfig.binaryPath, processEnv, { fresh: true }) and builds makeProviderMaintenanceCapabilities with updateExecutable = resolved.resolvedPath ?? resolved.command. Keep lockKey 'cursor-agent'. Pass it at :130 and :143. Thread the resolved command into getCursorParameterizedModelPickerUnsupportedMessage (CursorProvider.ts:762-790) and the not-installed message (:1033). In cliSetup/machine.ts:23, detect Cursor by `cursor-agent`. Tests: a CursorDriver/maintenance test with a temp PATH holding fake `agent` and `cursor-agent` executables asserts the update executable is cursor-agent, plus a CursorProvider message test. B) Registry deadlines (S). In AcpRegistrySupport.ts:66-78, remove the outer 30 s timeout and rely on the per-phase deadlines, or raise it above the phase sum (about 90 s) and keep it only as a backstop. Set the registry session-start default to the standard 120 s and fix the comment at providerOperationPolicy.ts:25-26. Test: a fake registry agent answering session/load after 40 s succeeds, and a hung session/new yields the phase message. C) Phase reporting (M). Add an optional `onStartupPhase: (phase) => Effect<void>` to AcpSessionRuntimeOptions and CodexSessionRuntimeOptions, invoked inside withStartupPhaseDeadline / withCodexStartupPhaseDeadline before the request. Adapters (CursorAdapter, AcpAdapter, GrokAdapter, CodexAdapter) emit session.state.changed { state: 'starting', reason: 'Authenticating with Cursor…' | 'Opening session…' | 'Resuming session…' }. ClaudeAdapter emits 'Loading Claude Code (plugins, MCP servers)…' before awaitCliInitialized when not initialized. In packages/contracts, add an optional session `statusDetail` (schema-only). In ProviderRuntimeIngestion.ts, set it on starting and clear it on ready/running/error/stopped in the session.state.changed lifecycle branch (around :2540-2600). Render it where client-runtime treats status 'starting' (threadWorkspaceViewModel.ts:470) in the working indicator. The Codex path already proves that pre-ready runtime events are ingested. Tests: an AcpSessionRuntime test for callback order initialize→authenticate→session/new, an ingestion projection/clear test and a view-model test. D) Optional: a Copilot start deadline (30 s create / 60 s resume) via providerStartupPhaseTimeoutDetail in CopilotAdapter.session.ts:272. Also an env multiplier (e.g. RYCO_PROVIDER_STARTUP_PHASE_TIMEOUT_SCALE) resolved in providerOperationPolicy and passed as phaseTimeouts/startupPhaseTimeouts. E) Textgen 180 s caps: handle in the textgen finding.
decisionReason: Items A, B and D are bug fixes or deadline plumbing with no security or protocol impact. Item C is an additive UX label that needs a small schema-only contracts field. The one product trade-off, lowering 180 s commit/PR text generation, is deferred to the separate textgen finding and should be decided there.
correction: The auditor said Cursor binary identity is not verified and suggested adding a probe-time `--version`/`about` identity check. #710 already added one: isCursorAgentAboutOutput (CursorProvider.ts:740), used at :1055 and tested. With pickers limited to 'ready' instances, a foreign `agent` cannot be picked for new sessions. The auditor also missed the uncovered `agent update` maintenance caller (CursorDriver.ts:48), which runs the Grok binary on this machine. The auditor called the registry 300 s default 'effectively unreachable' but missed that the same 30 s registry cap also cuts off the new 60 s session/load budget and replaces the actionable phase messages with a generic one.
